findings.title: Frontend Simulation Console Defaults to Client-Side Mock Random Walk Bypassing Real Backend Training

sink.surface: LossChart, MetricsComparisonBarChart, Champion AUC badge, Bank convergence statuses

execution_path: User visits /simulation or /live-operations (trainingMode defaults to 'mock')
User clicks 'Start Simulation' button
handleLaunchTraining calls startSimulatedTraining(selectedProfile)
startSimulatedTraining executes setTimeout timer loop with Gaussian noise math
State updates (setChampionAuc, setRoundHistory) render realistic-looking convergence curves
Zero network requests or PyTorch model updates are dispatched to the backend
findings.trigger: Clicking 'Start Simulation' button with default UI state or arriving with ?autostart=true
findings.current_behavior: Fabricates simulated round loss, AUC, and per-bank convergence curves completely in browser JavaScript memory using Math.random() and exponential decay formulas.
findings.claimed_or_implied_behavior: Executes multi-bank federated learning across participating bank nodes with differential privacy, gradient aggregation, and real model validation.
findings.user_visibility: Primary operator dashboard view. User observes animated training progress and convergence metrics labeled as live training.
evidence: frontend/src/pages/LiveOperationsView.tsx:L163: const [trainingMode, setTrainingMode] = useState<TrainingMode>('mock');
frontend/src/pages/LiveOperationsView.tsx:L799-L800: const gaussianNoise = (std: number) => std * Math.sqrt(-2 * Math.log(Math.random())) * Math.cos(2 * Math.PI * Math.random());
frontend/src/pages/LiveOperationsView.tsx:L811-L817: Mathematical formulas generating artificial AUC and Loss steps toward profile targets.
frontend/src/pages/LiveOperationsView.tsx:L1063: Button text displays 'Start Simulation' (without indicating mock or synthetic mode).
recommended_existing_targets: frontend/src/pages/LiveOperationsView.tsx :: wire 'Start Simulation' button directly to useCreateSimulation mutation
frontend/src/pages/LiveOperationsView.tsx :: isolate client-side simulation behind an explicitly labeled 'Offline Demo Mode' toggle
notes: A complete, working PyTorch federated training engine already exists on the backend.
Defaulting to 'mock' masks the real engine and presents artificial metrics as primary telemetry.

findings.title: Backend Startup Automatically Pre-Seeds Static Completed Simulation Run 'sim_fed_01'
execution_path: Backend server process starts up and imports simulation.py module
_seed_canonical_simulation() executes unconditionally at line 355
Populates _simulation_results['sim_fed_01'] with static 10 rounds, bank metrics, and Shapley payouts
Populates _simulation_events with 10 pre-computed round_complete payloads
Frontend LiveOperationsView fetches sim_fed_01 as activeSimId on initial load without running training
findings.current_behavior: Populates the in-memory/Redis simulation store with a synthetic completed run ('sim_fed_01') having hardcoded AUC 0.948, F1 0.892, Shapley distributions, and Intel SGX MRENCLAVE hashes.
findings.claimed_or_implied_behavior: Represents an actual completed consortium federated learning simulation session.
findings.user_visibility: Visible to any user opening the application on cold-boot before starting a new run.
evidence: backend/app/presentation/routers/simulation.py:L70-L140: canonical_banks dictionary containing hardcoded metrics.
backend/app/presentation/routers/simulation.py:L310: _simulation_results.set(sim_id, sim_doc)
backend/app/presentation/routers/simulation.py:L355: _seed_canonical_simulation() called at module level.
existing_real_alternative: Return 404 or empty state if no simulation has been executed yet, or explicitly mark 'sim_fed_01' with is_canonical_benchmark_reference: true
recommended_existing_targets: backend/app/presentation/routers/simulation.py:L355 :: gate seeding behind an explicit DEMO_SEED flag or annotate record metadata as CANONICAL_REFERENCE
notes: Seeding was added to ensure initial UI dashboards don't render empty errors, but it presents static historical results as active runtime state.

execution_path: Frontend application mounts and connects WebSocket to /ws/telemetry
Backend accepts connection and enters while True loop with asyncio.sleep(1.0)
Generates transactions using random.choice(typologies) and random.uniform(1500.0, 450000.0)
Sends JSON payload to client over WebSocket
Header renders 'Live WS (XXms)' and increments transaction counter
findings.trigger: Opening any page in the web application (Header maintains persistent WebSocket).
findings.current_behavior: Generates artificial transactions with random amounts, random bank IDs, and random fraud scores in an infinite sleep loop.
findings.claimed_or_implied_behavior: Represents live enterprise interbank payment traffic streaming from core banking systems.
findings.user_visibility: Top header bar of every page displays 'Live WS' indicator and transaction counter; ObservabilityPage displays live ticker.
evidence: backend/app/presentation/websockets/streaming_ws.py:L321-L322: typ, desc, sev, score = random.choice(typologies); bank = random.choice(banks)
backend/app/presentation/websockets/streaming_ws.py:L335: 'amount': round(random.uniform(1500.0, 450000.0), 2)
frontend/src/components/layout/Header.tsx:L33-L36: Renders 'Live WS' badge when connected to this synthetic stream.
recommended_existing_targets: backend/app/presentation/websockets/streaming_ws.py :: refactor endpoint to pull from Kafka/Redis stream when configured, and label as 'Simulated Telemetry' when running standalone demo
notes: The UI header shows green 'Live WS' badge, creating a strong impression that real interbank transactions are flowing.

findings.title: Design Partner Sandbox Synthesizes Model Predictions via Random Beta Distributions

sink.surface: Projected Financial & Labor Savings, False Alarm Reduction %, ROC-AUC / PR-AUC cards

execution_path: User visits /benchmarks (BenchmarkHubPage) and selects dataset/volume parameters
Frontend fires POST /api/v1/design-partner/benchmark
evaluate_reference_benchmark loads sample slice
Generates prediction probabilities using rng.beta(3.2, 1.4) and rng.beta(1.8, 2.2)
Calculates ROC-AUC and financial ROI metrics from Beta samples and returns JSON
Frontend renders annual savings ($USD) and dynamic ROI multiple
findings.current_behavior: Instead of executing inference with trained PyTorch model weights on the sample data, prediction probabilities are sampled from calibrated Beta distributions.
findings.claimed_or_implied_behavior: Evaluates reference benchmark models (PaySim, IEEE-CIS) against bank sample data to compute empirical accuracy and financial uplift.
findings.user_visibility: BenchmarkHubPage financial ROI panel and performance comparison cards.
evidence: backend/app/application/services/design_partner_service.py:L266-L267: y_prob_fl[fraud_idx] = rng.beta(a=3.2, b=1.4, size=len(fraud_idx))
backend/app/application/services/design_partner_service.py:L271-L272: y_prob_local[fraud_idx] = rng.beta(a=1.8, b=2.2, size=len(fraud_idx))
existing_real_alternative: backend/app/application/services/inference_engine.py :: run real forward pass using loaded PyTorch checkpoint
recommended_existing_targets: backend/app/application/services/design_partner_service.py:L256-L273 :: replace Beta random sampling with ModelService/InferenceEngine inference
notes: The service generates realistic-looking distributions for sub-second sandbox speed, but it bypasses real neural network inference.

findings.trigger: Visiting Model Governance console in a fresh environment.
findings.current_behavior: Fabricates two registered champion models with hardcoded version numbers, timestamps, and performance metrics when no models have been registered.
findings.claimed_or_implied_behavior: Lists authenticated, SR 11-7 compliant production models stored in the consortium registry.
findings.user_visibility: Model governance table displays hardcoded champions.

findings.title: In-Memory Ephemeral Storage Silently Replaces Redis with Zero Durability Warning

sink.surface: All simulation run persistence, event logs, rate limiters, session stores

execution_path: Backend starts with default configuration (redis_host = '')
RedisStore detects empty host and sets _global_redis_unavailable = True silently
Redirects all .set(), .get(), .push_list() operations to class-level Python dictionaries
UI operations succeed normally, but all state is destroyed on server restart
findings.trigger: Running backend without explicit REDIS_HOST environment variable.
findings.current_behavior: Silently uses in-memory dictionary storage while APIs and documentation imply durable Redis/Celery persistence.
findings.claimed_or_implied_behavior: Durable distributed caching and message broker for multi-tenant bank isolation.
findings.user_visibility: No direct error message. Users believe runs are permanently recorded.
evidence: backend/app/config.py:L56: # Leave redis_host empty to disable Redis and use in-memory storage silently.
backend/app/infrastructure/redis_store.py:L54-L57: self._redis_failed = True; RedisStore._global_redis_unavailable = True; return None
existing_real_alternative: backend/app/infrastructure/redis_store.py :: real Redis client when REDIS_HOST is configured
recommended_existing_targets: frontend/src/components/layout/Header.tsx :: display storage indicator if running in ephemeral mode
notes: In-memory fallback is helpful for zero-dependency local testing, but it must be surfaced explicitly rather than operating silently.

findings.title: Software TEE Attestation Driver Uses Artificial Sleeps and Static Seeds

sink.surface: Intel SGX Enclave Attestation Report, MRENCLAVE / MRSIGNER verification badges

execution_path: Simulation is launched with hardware_isolation_mode='intel_sgx'
SimulationService calls TEEDriver.create_enclave and TEEDriver.generate_attestation_report
Driver executes time.sleep(0.1) and time.sleep(0.05), computes SHA-256 of seed strings, and returns verified=True
SecurityPage renders 'Intel SGX Enclave: VERIFIED'
findings.trigger: Enabling SGX enclave in simulation parameters.
findings.current_behavior: Emulates SGX enclave attestation in pure software using sleep delays and static SHA-256 hashes.
findings.claimed_or_implied_behavior: Cryptographic hardware-isolated enclave remote attestation via Intel SGX / AWS Nitro.
findings.user_visibility: Security dashboard displays SGX attestation verification badge.
evidence: backend/app/infrastructure/security/tee_driver.py:L38: Docstring explicitly states SoftwareEmulatedTEEDriver for zero-hardware deployments.
backend/app/infrastructure/security/tee_driver.py:L53, L83: time.sleep(0.1) and time.sleep(0.05) artificial overhead delays.
existing_real_alternative: Check for /dev/sgx_enclave or /dev/nitro_enclaves; if absent, display mode as SOFTWARE_EMULATION_SANDBOX
recommended_existing_targets: backend/app/infrastructure/security/tee_driver.py :: surface is_emulated: True in AttestationReport and render 'Software Emulated' badge in UI unless real SGX device node exists
notes: The driver is well-structured as an emulator, but the UI renders it as 'Intel SGX Hardware Verified' without clearly indicating emulation.
